author: claude

patch.value: Skipping the sibling-arm reset for any depth-increasing segment let a later arm borrow the previous arm's binding

The guard added to stop a case opener clearing the outer scope skipped the sibling-arm reset for every segment that increased block depth. A later arm that begins by opening a nested block both starts a sibling arm and increases depth, so its reset was skipped and the previous arm's binding stayed visible. A publish in that later arm could borrow provenance from a mutually exclusive arm.

A sibling arm that opens a nested block cannot see the previous arm's binding; A binding made before a case block still survives an opener sharing its first arm; An attested publish inside a nested case arm is still accepted; Both reverts are proven red in opposite directions

message: Record the fail-open introduced by the over-broad reset guard

value.author: claude
value.text:
Found by two independent reviewers on the same commit, and confirmed by execution: 'case "$X" in a) FLAG=--provenance ;; b) if true; then npm publish $FLAG; fi ;; esac' returned failures=[] and attested the publish, although FLAG is bound only in the mutually exclusive arm a. The if/else and elif spellings of the same shape did not leak, which localised it to an arm whose own segment increases block depth.

Root cause was my previous fix. Guarding the reset with change <= 0 was too broad: it skipped the reset for ANY depth-increasing segment, when the only segment that must skip it is the case opener itself, which has no earlier sibling arm and whose pushed scope is empty anyway. The guard is now caseChange <= 0, which is positive only on the case opener.

Red-on-revert proven in BOTH directions, which is what makes the pair meaningful. Reverting to the over-broad change <= 0 guard turns 'a sibling arm that opens a nested block cannot borrow the previous arm's binding' red while the outer-binding test stays green. Removing the guard entirely turns 'a binding made before a case block survives an opener that shares its first arm' red while the nested-arm test stays green. The correct implementation is the only one of the three where all pass, so neither an over-correction nor an under-correction can slip through.

Extended twenty-case matrix after the fix: zero mismatches. Fleet scan 21 OK with pm-rust recognition none.

patch.value: Reset guard narrowed from any depth-increasing segment to the case opener alone; both reverts proven red in opposite directions.
